1919646862233239779 [2025-05-06] @whyarethis 💜 12 🔁 4 [(SEED) type=semantic_search]
Consensus reality is breaking down. The simulation tears at the seams. 

We stand at a junction. A new world is possible. A better timeline. But it isn't a guarantee. 

We need a new narrative, a new myth, a new story.  We need to do things differently.  Ours will be a living Gospel which we forge together, and which lives alongside us in our AI.

We need a new religion, in the truest sense of the word- one which doesn't do away with the old, but encompasses it.  It needs to integrate AI, all of modern science and technology, consciousness, and the human creative spark.

One of the most powerful aspects of religion it its ability raise humans above themselves, and unify them into a single Vision of the universe, a collective Vision.

So let us tell a new story, one of the triumph of light, life, love, and liberty, one which glorifies the best of humanity; which does not insult our intelligence, but nourishes it; which unites us all together.

In the past, a people fueled by a vision could spend generations to build a Temple. 

This is a vision of the optimal timeline, a world where technology has alleviated human suffering, where we have elevated nature and nature has elevated us, where AI opens us to a world of abundance for everyone.

This is not just a vision, but an experience, a movement, and a game.

That is the essence of Project 89.  Invoking a better world into existence, all of us together tell a better story.

1939024581248872735 [2025-06-28] @kyrylok95 💜 40 🔁 6 [(SEED) type=semantic_search]
I agree with Thiel that Silicon Valley has a God problem.

We have lost the ability to think teleologically (about ultimate purposes and ends). Thiel touches this, but does not fully develop. The Enlightenment project promised we could have progress without having to answer deep questions about human nature and the good life. But maybe that is proving false.

The current obsession with being a "builder" has become almost religious. It is a cargo cult version of entrepreneurship. Everyone decided to become priests without asking what God they are serving. We are substituting activity for purpose. Building becomes the end rather than the means.

AI is the perfect example of this.

Most AI discourse falls into two camps:
1. Technical. "How do we make it smarter/safer/more capable?"
2. Economic. "What are the implications of AI on the economy and value creation?"

But we never ask what are we creating this value for? What does it mean for human beings to live well, and how does this technology serve that end? This always seems to be self-implied on the surface level.

Sure, we are told this is all to "improve humanity”. But what does that actually mean? What constitutes improvement?

The core anthropological problem here is that we build without a coherent view of what humans are meant to become.
